messages.content: How to get nodes information for fabric test-de, the ip is 23.31.32.1?

function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide showing **how** to pull the full list of nodes that belong to the *“test‑de”* fabric from your APIC appliance whose management IP is 23.31.32.1.  
(The same approach works against any APIC/APIC‑SP instance – just swap out the host/IP.)

---

### 1️⃣ Log into the APIC’s REST API  

```bash
curl -sk \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -X POST \
     --data '{"aaaUser":{"attributes":{"name":"admin","pwd":"YOUR_PASSWORD"}}}' \
     https://23.31.32.1/api/
```

> This authenticates as **admin** (replace `YOUR_PASSWORD`).  
> You’ll receive a cookie (`APIC-cookie`) that you will reuse for subsequent calls.

If you prefer a browser, simply navigate to:
```
https://23.31.32.1/apic/ui/login.html
```
and log in normally.

---

### 2️⃣ Query the cluster for all nodes belonging to “test‑de”

Use the **Cluster Nodes** endpoint and add a filter so that only nodes inside the desired fabric appear.

```bash
curl -sk \
     -b "APIC-cookie=$COOKIE_VALUE" \
     "https://23.31.32.1/api/cluster/nodes.json?query-target-filter=eq(node.fab-name,\"test-de\")"
```

#### What each part does

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `https://23.31.32.1/api/cluster/nodes.json` | Returns JSON describing every node in the cluster. |
| `query-target-filter=` | Filters the result set. |
| `eq(node.fab-name,"test-de")` | Keeps only those nodes where the fabric name equals **test‑de**. |

> If you’re unsure whether the field name is exactly `fab-name`, try first without the filter to inspect the raw output, e.g.:

```bash
curl -sk -b "APIC-cookie=$COOKIE_VALUE" https://23.31.32.1/api/cluster/nodes.json
```

Then look under `"imdata"` → `"fvNode"` → `"attributes"` → `"fabricName"`.

---

### 3️⃣ Inspect the returned payload

A typical snippet looks like this:

```json
{
    "totalCount": 12,
    "imdata": [
        {
            "fvNode": {
                "dn": "uni/fabric/domains/test-de/epg-node-[10.0.0.101]",
                "attributes": {
                    "id": "101",
                    "fabricName": "test-de",
                    "role": "leaf",
                    ...
                }
            }
        },
        …
    ]
}
```

From here you can extract whatever fields you care about—e.g., `id`, `fabricName`, `role`, `serialNumber`, `model`.

---

### 4️⃣ Optional: Pull additional details per node

Once you’ve identified the node IDs, you can drill down further. Example: fetch detailed stats for node 101:

```bash
curl -sk -b "APIC-cookie=$COOKIE_VALUE" \
"https://23.31.32.1/api/node/mo/topology/pod-1/rn-phys-sys-101.json"
```

Replace `pod-1` & `rn-phys-sys-101` with the actual pod and node identifiers found earlier.

---

## TL;DR Quick Command Sequence

```bash
# 1) Authenticate
AUTH=$(curl -sk -d '{"aaaUser":{"attributes":{"name":"admin","pwd":"PASSWORD"}}}'
          https://23.31.32.1/api/)
COOKIES=$(echo $AUTH | grep -oP '(?<=>).*?(?=<)' | tr '\r\n' ';')

# 2) Get nodes in fabric “test-de”
curl -sk -b "$COOKIES" \
"https://23.31.32.1/api/cluster/nodes.json?query-target-filter=eq(node.fabricName,\"test-de\")"
```

*(Remember to replace `PASSWORD` with your real password.)*

That’s it! With the above request you now have a machine‑readable list of all nodes that live inside the **test‑de** fabric on the APIC at 23.31.32.1.
